title: Remark
body_md:
The present approach matches the spring model adopted among others by [\cite{mendez2014unstructured}].
Consider a virtual displacement $\delta V\in\mathbb{R}^2$ of a vertex $V$.
The latter corresponds to a the perturbation $\delta x = \varphi_V \delta V \in \mathbb{P}^1(\Gamma,\mathbb{R}^2)$, where $\varphi_V\in\mathbb{P}^1(\Gamma,\mathbb{R})$ is the nodal basis hat function of vertex $V$.
The corresponding nodal force $F_V$ applied to $V$ is defined as
\[
F_V \cdot \delta V = (f_{\textrm{str},h}, \delta x)_\Gamma,
\]
where $(f_{\textrm{str},h}, \delta x)_\Gamma$ is the virtual work corresponding to $\delta x$.
Using $(-)$ and $(+)$ to label entities associated to the 2 the edges touching $V$ and applying~\eqref{eq:ipp-f-str}, we get
\[
(f_{\textrm{str},h}, \delta x )_\Gamma = - (T\, \hat{t}_\Gamma\otimes\hat{t}_\Gamma, \nabla_\Gamma \delta x)_\Gamma = (T_{(+)} \hat{t}_{(+)} - T_{(-)} \hat{t}_{(-)}) \cdot \delta V,
\]
whence
\[
F_V = T_{(+)} \hat{t}_{(+)} - T_{(-)} \hat{t}_{(-)}.
\]
Therefore, $f_{\textrm{str},h}$ expresses the same information of a system of forces applied at nodes in which each edge applies the tension $T_E$ on the neighbouring nodes.

name: Comparison with the literature

title: Remark
body_md:
The discrete intrinsic Laplace operator can be applied to obtain a discrete curvature in $\mathbb{P}^1(\Gamma,\mathbb{R}^2)$. 
Let $V\in\mathcal{V}$, and use $(-)$, $(+)$ to label entities adjacent to $V$ from both sides.
Letting $\hat{k}_\Gamma = \Delta_{\Gamma} \Gamma$, from~\eqref{eq:disc-delta} we get, for all $ V \in \mathcal{V}$,
\[
\frac{1}{6}|E^{(+)}|\hat{k}_{(-)} + \frac{1}{3}(|E^{(-)}| + |E^{(+)}|)\hat{k}_V + \frac{1}{6}|E^{(+)}|\hat{k}_{(+)} = - |E^{(-)}|^{-1}(V- V^{(-)}) + |E^{(+)}|^{-1}(V^{(+)} - V),
\]
which, applying mass-lumping, reduces to
\[
\frac12 (|E^{(-)}|+|E^{(+)}|)  \hat{k}_V = \hat{t}_{(+)} - \hat{t}_{(+)},
\]
retrieving a well-established finite difference approximation of vector curvature.

title: Remark
body_md:
When $k=0$, the stability of the scheme\ref{eq:stokes.discrete} is no more guaranteed.
    A solution inspired by [\cite{bottiLoworderNonconformingMethod2019}] consists in adding a symmetric penalty term that penalizes the jump of reconstructed velocity at element-element interfaces~[\cite[Section 7.6]{dipietroHybridHighOrderMethod2020}].  
    This technique is applied in the numerical tests presented in Section~\ref{sec:num-tests}.
head: environment
name: Case $k=0$

label: rm:sliver.cuts
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rm:sliver.cuts}
The trajectory of the capsule is accurately reproduced without any special treatment for generated polygonal element with poor quality.
Sliver cuts are, however, the crucial challenge in the design of unfitted high-order schemes such as Cut-FEM or Cut-HHO,
which typically rely on specific techniques, such as Ghost Penalty, to enforce stability~[\cite{burmanCutFEMDiscretizingGeometry2015,burmanCutCellHybrid2019}].
Therefore, nothing prevents scheme~\eqref{eq:stokes.discrete}'s accuracy to be occasionally degraded in case of unfavorable cuts (see, for example, Fig.~\ref{fig:energy.balance}).
However, at least on the considered configuration, the noise on the approximation of velocity introduced by sliver cuts seems to have a low impact on the accuracy of the trajectory.
